meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I feel very frightened in my soul.
We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'letter (of the alphabet)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You don't read the small letters.
The child already knows all the letters.

examples.text: Женщина, вы мелкими буквами не читаете. Наша фирма в этом не виновата.
examples.trans: Ma'am, you don't read the small print. Our firm isn't to blame for that.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Lord' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'sin' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are afraid because of your sins!

examples.text: У нас с вами был сложный период. Сложный, чего греха таить.
examples.trans: You and I went through a rough patch. A rough one, no denying that.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sinful').
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты пишешь слишком медленно и грязно.
examples.trans: You write too slowly and messily.

examples.text: Она выглядит очень странно и грязно.
examples.trans: It looks very strange and dirty.
Why are you hovering over me?

examples.text: У меня на душе сильная тревога.
examples.trans: I have a strong anxiety in my soul.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'правлять'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to correct'.

examples.trans: It is hard to fix the mistakes of deceit.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to repent'.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I try very hard to write nicely.

examples.text: Вот теперь кусочки нарезаны красиво и аккуратно.
examples.trans: Now the pieces are cut beautifully and neatly.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('crooked, curved').

examples.trans: Look what a crooked letter turned out!

examples.text: Здесь был утрачен древний оригинал летописи.
examples.trans: Here the ancient original of the chronicle was lost.
Soon this chronicle will be taken back.
Go immediately and hide the chronicle!

examples.text: Подождите! Два дня — это же очень мало.
examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to pray'.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: два года назад = two years ago

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоятель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'abbot, prior' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Oh wow, praise from the abbot!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'меть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to go numb'.

examples.trans: My hand is going completely numb.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
This is some kind of mistake!
There are many serious mistakes in the case.

повезти.gloss: to be lucky (impersonal); to take (by vehicle)

meanings.note: impersonal, + dative: мне повезло = I was lucky; повезло! = what luck!

examples.trans: A lucky break: Tretyakov called back.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: всё получилось = it all worked out

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'хвала'). Common feminine noun meaning 'praise' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Oh wow, praise from the abbot!
What praise do you deserve, Konstantin?

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

стараться.gloss: to try, to make an effort

meanings.en: to try hard, to make an effort
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тараться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to make an effort', paired with 'постараться'.

examples.trans: He always tries to help his friends.

examples.text: Марина, зря вы стараетесь. Он никогда не уйдёт от своей Аллы Евгеньевны.
examples.trans: Marina, you're trying in vain. He will never leave his Alla Evgenyevna.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'траница'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'page' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And on the second page as well.
Open the book to page ten.
I will finish this page myself!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Он усердно работает над новым проектом.
examples.trans: He works diligently on the new project.
The students prepared hard for the exam.

examples.text: Ух ты! Как ты это сделал?
examples.trans: Wow! How did you do that?

examples.text: Да, мой топор. Ух ты! Как ты это сделал?
examples.trans: Yes, my axe. Wow! How did you do that?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
